title: Join the team: Kittitas Valley Fire and Rescue seeks new volunteers - NewsBreak
text:
By Monique Garcia ,
11 hours ago ELLENSBURG, Wash. — The Kittitas Valley Fire and Rescue is once again inviting residents of Kittitas County to apply for its annual volunteer program, a crucial backbone of the agency's emergency response efforts.
Applications are open to anyone living in the Kittitas County area, according to DJ Goldsmith, fire chief for Kittitas Valley Fire and Rescue. Additionally, the department offers a resident program where applicants can live at the fire station to gain firsthand experience and knowledge of fire service operations.
"We also have the resident program where folks can apply to become a resident and live here at the fire station to gain firsthand experience and knowledge of just how the fire service works. While serving the community, we find that very beneficial," Goldsmith said.
Volunteers must be legal adults with a valid driver’s license.
Goldsmith highlighted that training for volunteers is provided in-house. "If you're selected via volunteer, we put you through a volunteer recruit academy. If you want to do wildland as well, we provide that training for you. Additionally, we have EMS-only folks that we will sponsor to go and become an EMT, or you can be a full combat firefighter, which does both the structural, the wildland EMS, all facets of the position, and we provide all that training to our folks,” he said.
The station relies heavily on a volunteer force of about 70 to 80 individuals, which is vital to handling thousands of emergency calls each year, Goldsmith said.
"It is so important to have these folks, because they're the backbone of the agency. We really rely on our volunteers to provide the service to our community. Just because we're so large, we're over 280 square miles that we service as Kittitas Valley Fire Rescue, and over 1,200 square miles that we serve for the EMS. There's just a lot of ground to cover, and it's not feasible to have a full time staff to deal with that," Goldsmith said.
Goldsmith emphasized the importance of community dedication among volunteers. "We just need people dedicated, dedicated to the community, willing to help their neighbor in the worst times and needs. We look for our team member. We're a family here. We're a team, and we really look for those attributes when we're trying to select a volunteer,” he said.
This year, the department aims to recruit about 20 new volunteers. The deadline to apply is Sept. 30.
